'''Harris A. Lewin''',<ref name=pmid27956630/> an American biologist, is a professor of evolution and ecology and Robert and Rosabel Osborne Endowed Chair at the [[University of California, Davis]]. He is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=nas>{{cite press release |title=Harris Lewin Elected to National Academy of Sciences |publisher=[[Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology]] |date=30 April 2012 |url=https://www.igb.illinois.edu/article/harris-lewin-elected-national-academy-sciences |accessdate=July 14, 2020 }}</ref> In 2011, Lewin won the [[Wolf Prize in Agriculture]] for his research into cattle genomics.<ref name=nas /><ref name=sns /> Lewin chairs the working group for the [[Earth BioGenome Project|Earth BioGenome]] Project, a moonshot for biology that aims to sequence, catalog, and characterize the genomes of all of Earth’s eukaryotic biodiversity over a period of 10 years.<ref name=pmid29686065>{{cite journal |last1=Lewin |first1=Harris A. |last2=Robinson |first2=Gene E. |last3=Kress |first3=W. John |last4=Baker |first4=William J. |last5=Coddington |first5=Jonathan |last6=Crandall |first6=Keith A. |last7=Durbin |first7=Richard |last8=Edwards |first8=Scott V. |last9=Forest |first9=Félix |last10=Gilbert |first10=M. Thomas P. |last11=Goldstein |first11=Melissa M. |last12=Grigoriev |first12=Igor V. |last13=Hackett |first13=Kevin J. |last14=Haussler |first14=David |last15=Jarvis |first15=Erich D. |last16=Johnson |first16=Warren E. |last17=Patrinos |first17=Aristides |last18=Richards |first18=Stephen |last19=Castilla-Rubio |first19=Juan Carlos |last20=van Sluys |first20=Marie-Anne |last21=Soltis |first21=Pamela S. |last22=Xu |first22=Xun |last23=Yang |first23=Huanming |last24=Zhang |first24=Guojie |title=Earth BioGenome Project: Sequencing life for the future of life |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=24 April 2018 |volume=115 |issue=17 |pages=4325–4333 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1720115115 |pmid=29686065 |pmc=5924910 |bibcode=2018PNAS..115.4325L |doi-access=free }}</ref>
Lewin is a founding co-[[editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''[[Annual Review of Animal Biosciences]]'', first published in 2013.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev-av-1-012513-100001|title=Introduction|journal=Annual Review of Animal Biosciences|year=2013|volume=1}}</ref>

== Career ==
Lewin studied at [[Cornell University]] and earned his B.S. in Animal Science in 1979 and M.S. in Animal Breeding and Genetics in 1981. He was awarded his Ph.D. in Immunology from the [[University of California, Davis]] in 1984.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://biosci3.ucdavis.edu/Faculty/Profile/View/14515 |title=Harris Lewin {{!}} College of Biological Sciences |website=biosci3.ucdavis.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906231445/http://biosci3.ucdavis.edu/Faculty/Profile/View/14515 |archive-date=2015-09-06}}</ref><ref name=pmid27956630/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.igb.illinois.edu/labs/lewin/labweb/personnel/Harris.html |title=Harris A. Lewin, Ph.D. |website=www.igb.illinois.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812095427/http://www.igb.illinois.edu/labs/lewin/labweb/personnel/Harris.html |archive-date=2016-08-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://lewinlab.igb.uiuc.edu/Personnel/HarrisLewin.html |title=Personnel, Laboratory of Mammalian Genome Biology, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign |website=lewinlab.igb.uiuc.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080708185704/http://lewinlab.igb.uiuc.edu/Personnel/HarrisLewin.html |archive-date=2008-07-08}}</ref> He then worked at the [[University of Illinois]].<ref name=nas /> In 2003, he served as the founding director of the [[Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology]].<ref name=igb>{{cite web|url=http://www.igb.illinois.edu/about/history|title= History|website=[[Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology]]|access-date=7 November 2015}}</ref><ref name=sns>{{cite press release |title=Illinois professor awarded 2011 Wolf Prize in Agriculture |publisher=University of Illinois |date=15 February 2011 |url=https://news.illinois.edu/view/6367/205416 |accessdate=July 14, 2020 }}</ref> In 2009, he and a team of researchers fully sequenced the cow [[genome]].<ref name=sns />

Lewin served as vice chancellor for research at University of California, Davis from 2011 until 2016. In 2016 he returned to the faculty in the University of California, Davis Department of Evolution and Ecology and the Genome Center.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/research-vc-lewin-step-down/|title=Research VC Lewin to Step Down|website=UC Davis|date=9 February 2016|language=en|access-date=2017-07-27}}</ref> Lewin is a member of a group biologists that propose to sequence the DNA of all life on Earth.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pennisi |first1=Elizabeth |author-link=Elizabeth Pennisi |title=Biologists propose to sequence the DNA of all life on Earth |journal=Science |date=24 February 2017 |doi=10.1126/science.aal0824 }}</ref>

Lewin was senior author of a study that revealed one of the most prolific bulls in the history of Holstein cattle breeding, Pawnee Farm Arlinda Chief, had a lethal gene mutation estimated to have caused half million spontaneous cow abortions worldwide.<ref>{{cite press release |title=How a Genetic Mutation From 1 Bull Caused the Loss of Half a Million Calves Worldwide |publisher=UC Davis |date=13 October 2016 |url=https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/how-genetic-mutation-1-bull-caused-loss-half-million-calves-worldwide/ |accessdate=July 14, 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Zhang |first1=Sarah |title=The Dairy Industry Lost $420 Million From a Flaw in a Single Bull |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2016/10/the-dairy-industry-lost-420-million-from-a-flaw-in-a-single-bull/505616/ |work=The Atlantic |date=31 October 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newsweek.com/2016/11/25/dairy-cows-cattle-genetic-mutation-521152.html |title=One bull's genes gave 14 percent of U.S. dairy cows a deadly mutation |last=Main |first=Douglas |date=15 November 2016 |work=Newsweek }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=El ejemplar de toro que transformó la industria lechera mundial |trans-title=The bull that transformed the world dairy industry with 16,000 calves |language=Spanish |url=https://www.bbc.com/mundo/noticias-37826556 |work=BBC News Mundo |date=1 November 2016 }}</ref> Lewin collaborated with researchers from the Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique in France for a study that used RNA-sequencing to highlight problems with gene expression in cloned cattle.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/cow-gene-study-shows-why-most-clones-fail/|title=Cow Gene Study Shows Why Most Clones Fail|website=UC Davis|date=9 December 2016|language=en|access-date=2017-07-27}}</ref> In a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences,<ref name=pmid28630326>{{cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=Jaebum |last2=Farré |first2=Marta |last3=Auvil |first3=Loretta |last4=Capitanu |first4=Boris |last5=Larkin |first5=Denis M. |last6=Ma |first6=Jian |last7=Lewin |first7=Harris A. |title=Reconstruction and evolutionary history of eutherian chromosomes |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=3 July 2017 |volume=114 |issue=27 |pages=E5379–E5388 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1702012114 |pmid=28630326 |pmc=5502614 |bibcode=2017PNAS..114E5379K |doi-access=free }}</ref> Lewin and his colleagues used an algorithm to computationally recreate the chromosomes of the first eutherian mammal, the long-extinct, shrewlike ancestor of all placental mammals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/reconstruction-ancient-chromosomes-offers-insight-mammalian-evolution|title=Reconstruction of Ancient Chromosomes Offers Insight Into Mammalian Evolution|website=UC Davis|date=21 June 2017|language=en|access-date=2017-07-27}}</ref>

At the 48th World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos-Klosters, Switzerland, Lewin announced a landmark partnership between the [[Earth BioGenome Project]] and the Earth Bank of Codes to map the DNA of all the planet’s eukaryotes, some 1.5 million known species.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/earth-biogenome-project-sequence-all-life/|title=Earth BioGenome Project to Sequence All Life|website=UC Davis|date=23 January 2018|language=en|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.weforum.org/press/2018/01/new-partnership-aims-to-sequence-genomes-of-all-life-on-earth-unlock-nature-s-value-tackle-bio-piracy-and-habitat-loss/|title=New Partnership Aims to Sequence Genomes of All Life on Earth, Unlock Nature's Value, Tackle Bio-Piracy and Habitat Loss|website=World Economic Forum|access-date=2018-09-06}}</ref> Lewin was the lead author for a perspective paper published April 23, 2018 in the ''Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences'', "Earth BioGenome Project: Sequencing life for the future of life."<ref name=pmid29686065/> In the paper, the 24 interdisciplinary experts who comprise the Earth BioGenome Project Working Group, outline a roadmap and rational for the project, which is estimated to cost $4.7 billion and take ten years.<ref name=pmid29686065/>
